signal-by-street.title: Signal by street
signal-by-street.caption: How much of a six-way showdown the cards explain, by how many are known.

representation-ladder.title: Representation ladder
representation-ladder.caption: The same target, five encodings. Attention with positions wins; the embedding buys the ceiling, not the mechanism.
representation-ladder.alt: Horizontal bars from 13.1% (mean pool) to 40.0% (attention, 400 epochs).

card-model-convergence.title: Card model convergence
card-model-convergence.caption: Every early figure was a snapshot: the model was still improving at 320 epochs and flattened at 360-400.
card-model-convergence.alt: Line: R-squared rises from 25% at 20 epochs to 40% at 360, with the 60-epoch snapshot marked.

battery-error.title: Extremes battery
battery-error.caption: The converged card model predicts 2.7% for trip aces whose true equity is 91.8% — the failure a pooled R-squared could not show.
battery-error.alt: Grouped bars comparing true and predicted equity across seven verified extreme hands.

chips-ladder.title: Chips per hand
chips-ladder.caption: Same representation, same pooler, same league: the epsilon floor moves the agent from folding every hand to a mixed policy worth +11 to +13 chips per hand.
chips-ladder.alt: Horizontal bars with error bars: fold -0.6, product +1.8, eps 0.05 +3.7, eps 0.60 +11.3, +opponent model +12.9.

trunk-health.title: Dead trunk
trunk-health.caption: At the 600-scale reward every hidden unit was dead and the policy was a constant; the normalised reward revives 22 of 50.
trunk-health.alt: Two stacked bars: 0 of 50 live units under the 600-scale reward, 22 of 50 under the normalised reward.

monotonicity.title: Monotonicity
monotonicity.caption: Aggression should rise with equity. Suited junk is shoved while a small pair folds, and queens are called while an offsuit ace is shoved: 12 violations.
monotonicity.alt: Scatter of action (fold, call, raise) against true equity for twelve hole sets, showing inversions.

padding.title: Padding composition
padding.caption: A six-seat observation is 122 tokens; a preflop decision uses 14. The unmasked pool averaged the other 108 into every decision.
padding.alt: Stacked bar: 14 real tokens and 108 padding positions out of 122.

network-dead.title: Dead trunk
network-dead.caption: Under the 600-scale reward every hidden unit is dead: the two hidden columns are hollow rings with no wiring, while the input and the action layer are lit. The network outputs a constant.
network-dead.provenance: D-60, D-67, D-108 (measured: 0 of 50 and 0 of 50 units firing)
network-dead.alt: A four-column network diagram whose two hidden layers are open rings with no edges between them.

network-live.title: Live trunk
network-live.caption: With the normalised reward 23 of 50 hidden-1 units and 24 of 50 hidden-2 units fire, and the wiring between them is dense. Same architecture, same data, different reward scale.
network-live.provenance: D-67, D-108 (measured: 23 of 50 and 24 of 50 units firing)
network-live.alt: The same network diagram with most hidden units filled and dense edges between layers.

network-compare.title: Dead vs live trunk, side by side
network-compare.caption: Same 102-by-50 token learner, same league, two reward scales. Left: 0 of 50 units firing in both hidden layers. Right: 23 and 24 of 50.
network-compare.alt: Two network diagrams side by side: the left has empty hidden layers, the right has lit units and edges.

naive-vs-baselines.title: Naive model vs the baselines
naive-vs-baselines.caption: The naive model (flat numbers, plain stack) against each deterministic or random baseline, with a live token-embedding model beside it. Both beat the trivial opponents and both lose to the selective ones; the live model raises on three quarters of its decisions and is punished hardest.
naive-vs-baselines.provenance: trained for this figure at six seats (flat-numeric + naive-stack, 5,000 hands) and /tmp/foldloop/high; 1,000 hands per cell, 95% CI
naive-vs-baselines.alt: Grouped horizontal bars of chips per hand for twenty-four cells: two models against six opponents.
